title: Playing guitar with Sheik Colar in the 1950s
summary: He recalls jobs with Sheik and Henry Russ and not playing at Preservation Hall.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: You did play with Cheik because Henry Russ told me about that.
Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. I was back there with Cheik and Danny Barker coming in. Who was in that band when you were working with Cheik?
You were working with Cheik in the 50's sometime, huh?
Yeah, we was working back at, we was working back on Roachie Bridge in London Avenue. And Henry Russ was playing bass out with you, wasn't he?

We was back there with a group and they had a hole in the head, Walter, that boy we used to be with Fat Domino, his daddy. You know Walter. Yeah, Papoosh. Papoosh used to, Daddy used to be across the street. And Henry was down there with his brothers, never did get along with them brothers. You understand what I mean? That bass player and that guitar player, that Henry never could get along with them, that's why he never played with them. You understand what I mean? All that bunch was down there. I was down there with Cheik and this bunch.
I've been with the boys all right.
You understand? And we'd be down there riffing and playing all that kind of stuff. We had all the mumber up. We had the crowd, we'd do all the crowd down there where we was.
You had all those mumber on?

It used to be like a patio. We'd be playing that. They was playing like closed-end joints. You know what I'm saying? But they used to come down there with Cheik and da da Sheik. You played a lot with Cheik? I played a good bit with Cheik. You played guitar did it?
I played guitar with Cheik. But Howard too. You never played at Non-Preservation Hall down there? Where's that?
Preservation Hall in the past quarter?
No, I didn't. Once I played down at one carnival I'd be, no I ain't never played.
